transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I feel drained all the time, like I never have the energy to get through work or even enjoy the things I used to. It's just gotten to a point where everything feels like a massive effort, and I knew I needed to talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has this happened before as a separate period in your life? Have there been times in between when you felt back to your usual self?

This heavy, drained feeling has been going on continuously for a little over two years now, starting around the middle of my second year of college. There haven't been any breaks or periods where I felt back to my usual self—it's just been a constant, uninterrupted struggle.

Over these past two years, have you felt down or hopeless most days, or has the main problem been feeling physically and mentally exhausted without much sadness? Which of those has been more true for you?

It’s actually a mix of both. Along with the constant physical and mental exhaustion, I feel this dull heaviness in my chest, like a gray filter over everything that leaves me feeling numb and sad. I also feel really hopeless about the future, so it's definitely much more than just being tired.
During these two years, have there been stretches of at least 2 months when your mood and energy felt mostly back to normal, or has the depression been present nearly every day the whole time?
No, there haven't been any breaks like that at all. It has been present nearly every single day for the entire two years, without any periods where my mood or energy returned to normal.

During these two years, was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when your depression became much worse than usual, with symptoms like losing interest in almost everything, major sleep or appetite changes, trouble concentrating, or thoughts of death? Or has it stayed at about the same low level the whole time?

It has stayed at pretty much the same low level the entire time without any sudden, severe spikes. I haven't experienced things like appetite changes or thoughts of death, just that same constant, exhausting gray filter and low energy dragging me down steadily for the last two years.

During this two-year period, have you also had at least two of these most days: poor appetite or overeating, insomnia or sleeping too much, low self-esteem, poor concentration or trouble making decisions, or feeling especially hopeless? Which ones?

Yes, I’ve definitely struggled with low self-esteem and hopelessness. I constantly feel like a fraud who isn't as smart or capable as my peers at work or school, and when I think about the future, it just looks like an endless, exhausting grind that will never get any better.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronically depressed mood with persistent low energy for over two years, present nearly every day without remission longer than 2 months. During this period, they also endorse low self-esteem and hopelessness, meeting core features of persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia). There is no history of distinct major depressive episodes with clear worsening, and no evidence provided for mania or hypomania.
